summary: Red team of part 1 of the Algebraic K-theory area: eight roadmaps and 109 stages (MotivicEtaleKTheory 21, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory 15, KTheoryLowDegrees 15, K2SymbolsBrauer 14, ArithmeticKTheory 12, StableHomotopyKTheory 12, BorelRegulators 10, KTheoryFiniteLocalFields 10), with the integrated decompositions of GeneralAlgebraicKTheory and StableHomotopyKTheory, read against part 2 and the whole atlas. There are 49 findings: 6 high, 33 medium and 10 low. Five high findings are unplanned inputs to a main theorem. (1) Quillen's finite generation (N.3, R.1) needs the Tits building, Solomon–Tits, the Steinberg module, the rank filtration and Borel–Serre duality; the 'finite-type homotopy' input the stages name does not bound H_*(Γ, St). (2) M.7's Quillen–Lichtenbaum deduction needs the Beilinson–Lichtenbaum form of the norm-residue theorem, which M.5 does not state. (3) The real 2-primary calculation of M.7 and N.5 needs Suslin's K(ℝ) theorem and real topological K-theory. (4) BGL(R)⁺ as the group completion (H.3, H.4) needs H-space homology Whitehead theory and obstruction theory. (5) Borel's regulator theorem (R.5) needs τ(SL₁(D)) = 1, strong approximation and a division algebra with prescribed invariants. The sixth high finding is an ordering error: Waldhausen additivity sits in K.4, after the H.5 delooping whose proof needs it, and the packets' own links make this a cycle. The medium findings are of three kinds. Missing inputs: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem for U.4; Nesterenko–Suslin/Totaro and Suslin reciprocity for M.4; the recognition theorem for universal central extensions; the levelwise-fibration realisation theorem; Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectra of chain complexes; Milnor-square excision; rational Hurewicz for H-spaces; Green's theorem and Atiyah–Segal for L.1; the local Hilbert pairing for L.3/L.6; log structures for L.5. Wrong or missing prerequisites: T.5, T.4/T.3, U.4, K.3, K.5–K.7, K.6, M.5d, M.5, R.4, S.4. Duplicates: N.3:ranks/R.3, M.3/T.7, T.5 in N.2/N.6/N.8, N.4/B.1, N.8/B.3, V.1/T.1, R.2/ALS.5, T.4 with Tau Ceti curve work, and StableHomotopyKTheory with Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology. One acceptance test is false: K₀VB of the affine line with a doubled origin is not ℤ, since Pic is ℤ; the test copies a misprint in K-book V Remark 3.4.2. One library claim: Tau Ceti already has exact structures, ExactK0 and Proj_fg(A). The low findings are ownership, edge and presentation points. The coordinator extracted 17 of the papers routed to this area; their routes are not covered.

findings.claim: Quillen's proof of finite generation of K_n(O_F), which N.3:finite-generation must reproduce, rests on objects and theorems that no atlas stage plans and the libraries lack: the spherical Tits building T_n(F) and the Steinberg module St_n(F) = H̃_{n-2}(T_n(F); Z); the Solomon–Tits theorem (T_n(F) is a wedge of (n-2)-spheres); Quillen's rank filtration of Q(P(A)) for a Dedekind domain A, whose relative terms are H_*(Aut(P), St(P⊗F)); and finite generation of H_*(GL_n(O_F), St_n(F)), which comes from Borel–Serre duality (St is the dualizing module), not from the 'finite-type homotopy' of arithmetic groups: St_n(F) is a free abelian group of infinite rank, so finiteness of BΓ alone does not bound H_*(Γ, St). The only arithmetic-group input named is 'finite-type homotopy', and it is claimed twice, by N.3:finite-generation and by R.1.

findings.claim: M.7 deduces Quillen–Lichtenbaum 'from M.5 and M.6', but M.5 states only the Milnor-K (Bloch–Kato) form of the norm-residue theorem for fields. The deduction needs the Beilinson–Lichtenbaum form: for a smooth scheme X over a field k with 1/m ∈ k, H^n(X, Z/m(i)) → H^n_et(X, μ_m^{⊗i}) is an isomorphism for n ≤ i, with Z/m(i) identified with τ_{≤i}Rα_*μ_m^{⊗i}. This is what identifies the finite-coefficient E_2 page of M.6's spectral sequence with (truncated) étale cohomology. Its equivalence with the Milnor-K form is a separate theorem (Suslin–Voevodsky 2000, Geisser–Levine 2001). No stage states it, although the Clausen–Mathew extraction marks it 'planned' in M.5/M.7 and tells its Part II to import 'M.5 (norm residue and its Beilinson–Lichtenbaum form)'. The libraries have no motivic cohomology.

findings.claim: R.5 must prove Borel's regulator theorem, but the arithmetic inputs of Borel's proof have no planned owner or no edge into R.5. Borel evaluates the covolume by integrating a rational invariant form over the compact quotient H(R)/Γ_H, where H = SL_1(D) and D is a central division algebra over k of degree m+1 that splits at every archimedean place. The proof needs four inputs. (a) The Tamagawa number τ(SL_1(D)) = 1 (Weil; rationality suffices), together with the local volumes of SL_n(o_v), which give the Euler factors of ζ_k(m+1). (b) The existence of such a D: the Brauer sequence, plus a cyclic extension with prescribed local degrees. (c) Strong approximation for H. (d) Compactness of H(A)/H(k). No atlas stage computes any Tamagawa number: AA.2 excludes it, and the libraries have none. AA.4 (strong approximation) and ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 (the Brauer sequence) are not ancestors of R.5, and ClassFieldTheory excludes the Grunwald–Wang-type input. R.5's only prerequisites are AL.1 and R.4. The roadmap's references cite Borel (1974), which proves the rank theorem, not the regulator theorem. R.6 plans the adelic/Tamagawa framework after R.5, so R.5 cannot use it.

findings.claim: M.4 must prove 'field Milnor K-theory on the diagonal', i.e. CH^n(F,n) ≅ K_n^M(F) (Nesterenko–Suslin, Totaro). Building the inverse map needs two things. The first is the Milnor K-theory norm N_{E/F}: K^M_n(E) → K^M_n(F), with Kato's theorem that it does not depend on the generators chosen. The second is Suslin's reciprocity law Σ_w N_{κ(w)/F} ∂_w(x) = 0 for x ∈ K^M_{n+1}(F(C)), C a smooth proper curve over F. The norm is owned by K2SymbolsBrauer T.4 (RS-28), which is not an ancestor of M.4. Suslin's reciprocity law in degrees above 2 is planned nowhere: T.4 plans only the K_2 → K_1 Weil reciprocity. The libraries have no Milnor K-theory.

K2SymbolsBrauer:T.4: 'Prove the Bass–Tate sequence for F(t) and use it to construct Milnor transfers and their transitivity. … For a proper regular curve prove Weil reciprocity in the form ∏_{x∈X^{(1)}} N_{k(x)/F}(∂_x{f,g})=1.' Source: Totaro, Milnor K-theory is the simplest part of algebraic K-theory, K-Theory 6 (1992) 177–189 (author copy https://www.math.ucla.edu/~totaro/papers/public_html/milnor.pdf, read 2026-09-24), §3, p. 183: 'The map CH^n(F,n) → K^M_n(F) is defined by sending p to N_{κ(p)/F}{x_1,…,x_n} … N_{E/F}: K^M_n(E) → K^M_n(F) … is the norm homomorphism defined by Milnor [6], Bass-Tate [1], and Kato [5]. (Kato was the first to show that it was well-defined, independent of a choice of generators for E over F.)'; pp. 183–184: 'Suslin's reciprocity law ([8]) asserts that for any x ∈ K^M_{n+1}(K), Σ_{w∈P(D)} N_{κ(w)/F} ∂_w x = 0 in K^M_n(F).' findings.claim: No stage plans the realization theorem for levelwise fibration sequences of simplicial spaces, and the libraries lack it. The theorem: if X. → Y. → Z. is a sequence of simplicial spaces with each X_n → Y_n → Z_n a fibration and each Z_n connected, then Ω|Z.| → |X.| → |Y.| → |Z.| is a homotopy fibration (Waldhausen 1978, Lemma 5.2; Bousfield–Friedlander, Thm B.4). It is the key step in proving the relative S.-fibration (Weibel V.1.7, Waldhausen Prop. 1.5.5), on which the S.-delooping, Waldhausen relative K-theory (K.5) and the localization theorem rest. H.2 plans only the diagonal/iterated-realization comparison and the levelwise-equivalence theorem. Its nodes supply only Quillen's quasi-fibration lemma for diagrams over a nerve, which is a different statement. The GeneralAlgebraicKTheory node treats the theorem as an unread import.

Node H.2/quasi-fibration-lemma is stated for 'i ↦ X_i a functor to topological spaces' over BI whose transition maps are homotopy equivalences. Weibel K-book V (Kbook.V.pdf, read 2026-09-24), p. findings.claim: No stage plans Bass's Mayer–Vietoris sequence for a Milnor square, and the libraries lack it. The sequence is Milnor's K₁–K₀ sequence (Weibel III Thm 2.6) continued into negative K-theory (III Thm 4.3; Bass XII.8.3); equivalently, nonconnective K-theory satisfies excision in degrees ≤ 0 and is surjective in degree 1. Clausen–Mathew–Morrow use it in Prop. 4.34, and their extraction records item /076 as 'planned' in K.5 and K.6, but neither stage plans it. K.5's node states only K₀(R, I) ≅ K₀(I), the Suslin and Suslin–Wodzicki criteria and 'K₁ excision iff I = I²', with no Mayer–Vietoris sequence and nothing in negative degrees; K.6's nodes contain no Milnor square. K.6 must also 'identify negative groups of rings with Bass's construction', yet no stage defines Bass's contracted-functor groups.

findings.claim: R.3 converts the primitive cohomology calculation into K-group ranks by 'rational Hurewicz'. No stage plans it, or the Hopf-algebra structure theory it rests on. The only planned Hurewicz theorem is Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stage 8, the integral theorem for (n−1)-connected spaces, which does not apply to BGL(O)^+. Mathlib has only the definition of primitive elements and lists Milnor–Moore as a TODO. R.3's computation of the compact duals 'using the classical groups and their fibrations' also needs the Serre spectral sequence. AlgebraicTopology Stage 5 plans it over finite CW bases, but that stage is not an ancestor of R.3.

Source: L. Hesselholt and I. Madsen, 'On the K-theory of local fields', Ann. of Math. 158 (2003) 1–113, arXiv:math/9910186v2 (read 2026-09-24), Introduction pp. 4–5: 'A log ring (R, M) is a ring R with a pre-log structure ... The groups TR^1_*(A|K; p) form a log differential graded ring whose underlying log ring is A = O_K with the canonical pre-log structure given by the inclusion α: M = A ∩ K^× → A' and 'The algebraic structure described here makes sense for any log ring (R, M), and we show that there exists a universal example: the de Rham-Witt pro-complex with log poles W·ω*_(R,M). findings.evidence: Roadmap: MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.7: 'At 2 with real places, prove the corrected long exact sequences and extension data'; M.7 handoff row: 'At real dyadic places retain modified cohomology and extension data in the degree-specific arithmetic output.' findings.claim: R.4 plans to 'Construct ... the regulator covolume' and to prove 'independence from the chosen integral basis'. Mathlib already has the covolume of a full ℤ-lattice in a finite-dimensional real space, its independence of the fundamental domain, and its determinant formula for any ℤ-basis. The Dirichlet regulator, the j = 1 analogue, is defined as exactly that covolume. The stage's own work is the image lattice and its normalisation, not the covolume.

Prove that the image is a full lattice, with independence from the chosen integral basis up to the designated orientation/sign convention.'
